weakest_points_in_cycle: Assumes SINDy + multi-start differential–evolution exhaustively enumerates *all* polynomial vector fields that match the data (A-completeness). Completeness hinges on the unproven assumption that the true ODE lies inside the ±3, degree-3 integer-coefficient box; if this is false, both the A-claim and B-claim collapse.

Class-A enumerates only integer-valued coefficients; if the hidden generator contains any non-integer (irrational or even rational) constants, completeness claim fails and B cannot certify the true law.

Unjustified assumption that Savitzky–Golay (order-5, GCV window) keeps the L2 derivative error ≤ 5 % everywhere; if violated the MILP search space misses the true generator, collapsing both A- and B-claims.

Class-A integral collocation imposes |∫x dt − w Φ(X̄)·c| ≤ ε, equating ∫x dt with w·F(X̄); for nonlinear systems this surrogate is mathematically wrong, so the true generator will often violate the MILP constraints and be pruned—undercutting the completeness claim.
final_weakest: The entire completeness claim rests on the unproven premise that the true dynamics, once expressed in the 6-dimensional Takens delay-embedding, is still a sparse cubic polynomial with small integer coefficients; if this fails, the exhaustive grid search is exhaustive over the wrong space and Class-A coverage collapses.
failure_signature: The cycle addressed the stall caused by an unverified sparsity-and-integrality assumption: the Class-A exhaustive grid search was defined over a ±3, degree-3 integer-coefficient polynomial box whose adequacy as a search space for the true gp140 ODE generator was never established.
resolution_move: Replaced the unverified integer-coefficient box with a two-stage apparatus that first uses data-driven coefficient-range estimation to bound the search space empirically, then applies a formal coverage certificate (a residual-gap test) as a gate that must pass before Class-A completeness is asserted.
what_survived: The structural claim that a Takens delay-embedding of dimension 6 is a valid coordinate system for reconstructing the hidden attractor, and that SINDy-style sparse regression is a legitimate candidate-generation step within that embedding.
what_opened: Whether the residual-gap certificate itself is tight enough—i.e., whether the gap threshold can be set without introducing a new unverified assumption about noise floor and derivative-estimation error jointly.

proof_object_delta.after: A data-driven coefficient-range estimator paired with a residual-gap gate that must be satisfied before Class-A coverage is declared, replacing the bare grid-search with a certifiable search-space construction step.

weakest_points_in_cycle: Assumes the invariant-measure Fisher Information Matrix is strictly convex, guaranteeing <1e-4 parameter boxes; known counter-examples (divergence-free additions) leave the FIM rank-deficient, undermining both A-fit exhaustiveness and B-filter precision.

The entire Class-B mechanism relies on the mathematically false premise that Maximal Lyapunov Exponents (MLE) are altered by smooth coordinate warps (diffeomorphisms). MLE is invariant under C^1 diffeomorphisms, meaning the proposed filter will fail to reject adversarial coordinate warps.

Class-B mathematical flaw: Constant Jacobian Trace is invariant under volume-preserving diffeomorphisms and is not universally constant across true chaotic systems (e.g., Rössler), making it both blind to Framer-gaming and prone to rejecting real physics.

The chosen physical prior (Dimensional Consistency) is mathematically incompatible with the chosen held-out substrate (Rössler attractor). The Rössler equations inherently mix dimensions if state variables are assigned physical units, guaranteeing the unconditional rejection of the true generator and falsifying the B-claim.

The mathematical assumption that a non-dimensionalized nonlinear chaotic substrate (Rössler) recovered via dimensionless integer coefficients (LLL) can survive a strict Dimensional Consistency Audit. It is self-falsifying and guarantees rejection of the true physical system.

Fundamental logic contradiction in Method B: proposing a C1-diffeomorphism-invariant property (Persistent Homology Betti numbers) to reject C1-diffeomorphism coordinate warps, rendering the filter completely blind to the exact exploits it claims to prevent.
final_weakest: The thesis is mathematically self-falsifying: by specifying a single scalar observable as the input contract, it forces Method A to perform a non-affine state-space reconstruction, which geometrically injects the exact fluctuating positive divergence that Method B's Strict Dissipativity prior is designed to definitively reject.
failure_signature: The cycle addressed the stall caused by an inadequate input contract: a single scalar observable forced Method A into non-affine state-space reconstruction, injecting positive divergence that Method B's Strict Dissipativity prior was structurally guaranteed to reject.

weakest_points_in_cycle: The B-claim mathematically fails because it asserts all non-affine C1-diffeomorphisms inject an oscillating Jacobian log-determinant time-derivative that violates the strict negative divergence threshold. This completely ignores volume-preserving non-affine diffeomorphisms (like nonlinear shears) where the determinant is globally 1, the log-determinant is 0, and the divergence is perfectly preserved—allowing adversarial non-physical warps to effortlessly bypass the Method B filter.

Method-A takes a scalar observable that necessarily requires a non-affine Takens-style reconstruction, yet Method-B imposes a Strict Global Liouville Dissipativity prior whose validity is broken by that very reconstruction; the thesis ignores the v2.6 ‘input-contract / filter compatibility’ ban and therefore self-falsifies.

Method B rests on “Strict Global Liouville Dissipativity” (max ∇·f < 0) as a decisive law-certification gate; but global negativity cannot be proven from finitely-sampled noisy trajectories and is not guaranteed even for the true generator under small modelling error, so the filter can both reject truth and admit cleverly warped fakes.

weakest_points_in_cycle: The thesis hinges on the claim that a time-averaged Lyapunov-sum test (Σλi<0 with one ≈0 exponent) will reliably separate the true generator from the huge over-fit polynomial family emitted by Weak-LLL, even though adding small linear sink terms or having estimator variance at finite T can make many wrong candidates pass, while noise-induced bias can make the true model occasionally fail.

Assumes equality of finite-sample Betti numbers (β0,β1) between noisy data and simulated trajectory is a reliable, low-variance discriminator; in practice Betti estimates fluctuate with noise level, sampling density, and Vietoris-Rips scale, so both false negatives (true law rejected) and false accepts (distinct ODE with homeomorphic attractor) remain probable.

Core assumption that selecting only the P highest-power PSD peaks and setting each weak-form test radius r_k ∝ 1/f_dom_k preserves ≥95 % of the algebraic rank that a full logarithmic sweep would give for every continuous-chaos system. Empirically unverified and contradicted by broadband / intermittent chaos examples; if false, Method A fails to emit the full behavioural-equivalence set, violating the charter.

The core assumption that all weak-form integrals with support larger than the first zero-crossing of the scalar autocorrelation (τ_auto) are linear combinations of shorter-window integrals—hence add no new rank—is unproven and demonstrably false on many broadband chaotic signals; if the assumption fails, Method-A misses basis rows and the entire ABW pipeline collapses.

The entire bias-correction scheme depends on a sharp noise-only frequency band (f>f_noise) containing zero signal power, an assumption empirically false for broadband chaotic flows; if even small signal energy leaks above f_noise the rank guarantee and the claimed unbiased coefficient recovery both fail.
final_weakest: Method A relies on a catastrophic assumption that continuous chaotic substrates possess a sparse set of discrete 'dominant frequencies' (PSD peaks). Broadband chaos does not. Restricting Weak-form LLL test radii to these pseudo-peaks acts as a narrow filter that annihilates the broadband nonlinear information, collapsing the column space, and making the data matrix severely rank-deficient.
failure_signature: The cycle addressed the stall caused by the PSD-peak frequency selection heuristic, which assumed broadband chaotic substrates possess a sparse set of dominant frequencies sufficient to preserve algebraic rank in the Weak-form LLL test radius assignment.
resolution_move: Abandoned the PSD-peak radius assignment rule and replaced it with a logarithmic sweep apparatus that samples test radii densely across the full frequency band, eliminating the sparse-peak filter that collapsed the data matrix column space.
